prompt:
consider an isentropic diffuser that have subsonic flow in all cross sections. assume that P_0(stagnation pressure in upstream) and P_b(back pressure in downstream) are constant. now we increase the lenght of diffuser which it means we increase the cross section area . assume that the flow still subsonic.Now, how should we justify this contradiction that although the pressure ratio of (P_b/P_0) remains constant so the Mach should not change, on the other hand, we know that the cross-sectional area has increased and the Mach should decrease at the outlet of this diffuser.
Is there a way to fix this? Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response.
judge_reasoning: Candidate 2 most directly addresses the “fix” by noting that changing diffuser geometry can force other flow quantities to adjust (e.g., upstream conditions/mass flow) to keep the exit state consistent with the imposed pressure ratio, though it remains somewhat qualitative. Candidate 3 correctly observes that in the ideal isentropic case a fixed downstream-to-stagnation pressure ratio implies a fixed exit Mach, but then tries to “reconcile” by appealing to subtle variable changes/averaging without giving a consistent mechanism. Candidate 1 talks about stagnation/pressure distribution in a vague way and does not clearly resolve the contradiction using the isentropic pressure–Mach relation, leaving key logic gaps. Candidate 4 effectively repeats the contradiction in an internally inconsistent way (asserting Mach decreases at the outlet despite a constant pressure ratio), so it does not provide a valid resolution.
